moroccan_darija.notes: Heaviest Berber/Tamazight + French + Spanish influence. Often unintelligible to Mashreq Arabs.

algerian.notes: Heavy French code-switching, some Berber substrate.

tunisian.notes: Closer to Mashreq than Moroccan; French-Italian heritage.

casual_social.description: Default for Darija social — extremely French-blended; almost unintelligible to Egyptians/Khaleejis.

professional_casual.description: French-Arabic blend on LinkedIn Maghreb — French often dominant.

grammar_quirks: Moroccan 'ka-' present tense prefix (kaymshi = he goes)
Heavy French verb borrowings with Arabic conjugation

code_switching_patterns.french_in_arabic: Default — Maghrebi Darija sentences routinely contain 30-50% French. 'Je vais à l'école' could equally be 'غادي للمدرسة' or 'غادي à l'école'.
rules: If brand is Maghreb-only, French-Arabic blend is native.
If pan-Arab, switch to MSA — Mashreq audiences cannot parse Darija.

do_not_use: Mashreq Arabic markers (ده، دي، إزاي، شو، وش) — wrong family
Pan-Arab MSA in Darija casual content — feels stiff and foreign

example_translations.note: Pan-Maghreb campaigns are rare — produce per-country versions.
